title: Stunt Rank
pageTitle: Describe the Data Using the Median
covers: ordering data to find the median for odd and even counts, and why the median resists outliers
cert: finding the median of odd and even data sets and explaining why it resists outliers

intro.caption: Lesson 2-3 — the median. Dex claims his middle stunt score proves he is the most consistent skater on the channel. Mei checks his math before the finals.

balloons.t: My last five stunt scores were 82, 45, 95, 50, and 74. The middle one is 95! I'm basically pro!
I replayed that 45-point wipeout three times. You did NOT sort the list!
95 is sitting right in the middle of my list! Why won't you count it?
Because the median is the middle AFTER you order the numbers from least to greatest!

pages.caption: The middle of an unsorted list is meaningless. Always order the data from least to greatest first.

balloons.t: Line up Dex's five scores from smallest to largest, then grab the middle one.
Dex just did a sixth stunt and scored 66! Now there are 6 scores — two sit in the middle!
Do we pick the bigger one? Tell me we pick the bigger one.
My mean stunt score is 54! That beats almost everyone!
Nice try, Max. Four of your five stunts were in the 40s. One lucky 98 dragged your mean way up!
Finals round! Sort the board, handle the even count, and see who is truly typical.
No unsorted shortcuts on my watch!
Okay, 70 is way more honest than 95 — and I still beat Max fair and square!

win.caption: To find the median, order the data from least to greatest first. For an odd count, take the exact middle; for an even count, average the two middle numbers. Unlike the mean, the median resists extreme outliers.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Sort Then Find
hints: Conceptual: the median is the middle value of an ORDERED data set — never an unsorted list.
Procedural: arrange all 5 numbers from least to greatest, then pick the 3rd value.

steps: With 5 values, the 3rd value is the middle: median = 25 (not 40!).

items.q: Tap Dex's 5 stunt scores in order from least to greatest.
items.fb: Start with the smallest score (45) and work up to the largest (95).

items.label: Now what is the true median of Dex's 5 stunt scores?

fb.msg: 95 was in the middle BEFORE sorting. Always sort least to greatest first.
82 is the 4th score when sorted, not the 3rd (middle).

items.fbDefault: Look at the sorted list: 45, 50, 74, 82, 95. Which score sits in the exact middle?

gates.pass: Sorted: 45, 50, 74, 82, 95. The true median is 74 — sorry, Dex, not 95!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Even Count
gates.prompt: Dex adds a 6th score of 66. The 6 sorted scores are now: 45, 50, 66, 74, 82, 95.
hints: Conceptual: when there is an even number of values, there is no single middle number — two values share the middle.
Procedural: find the 3rd and 4th values, add them together, and divide by 2.

steps: The two middle values are 14 and 22.

items.label: Median of 45, 50, 66, 74, 82, 95:
items.aria: median of the six stunt scores

fb.msg: 66 is only the lower of the two middle values. Find the halfway number between 66 and 74.
74 is only the upper of the two middle values. Average 66 and 74.
140 is 66 + 74. Remember to divide by 2 to find the halfway point.

items.fbDefault: Average the two middle scores (66 and 74): add them, then divide by 2.

items.q: Why is the median 70 even though 70 is not one of Dex's six scores?

options.t: With an even count, the median is halfway between the two middle values
Someone forgot to type 70 into the list
options.fb: All 6 scores are there. An even count has no single middle item, so we average the middle pair.

options.t: You always round down to the nearest ten
options.fb: We do not round to tens; we find the exact halfway value between 66 and 74.

gates.pass: Halfway between 66 and 74 is 70! Half of Dex's scores are below 70 and half are above.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Fix the Bragging Board
gates.prompt: Max Maxwell's 5 stunt scores are 40, 42, 44, 46, 98. His mean is 54, and he claims he usually scores over 50.
hints: Conceptual: one extreme outlier pulls the mean toward it, but the median stays with the middle of the group.
Procedural: find the middle score of Max's 5 ordered scores, then compare it to the mean of 54.

steps: Mean = (10 + 11 + 12 + 13 + 54) ÷ 5 = 100 ÷ 5 = 20, even though four scores are 13 or less!
Median = 12 (the 3rd value), which honestly shows a typical score.
worked.q: For 10, 11, 12, 13, 54, which measure better shows a typical score?

items.label: What is Max's median score (40, 42, 44, 46, 98)?

fb.msg: 54 is the mean, which got pulled up by 98. The median is the middle value.
98 is the maximum outlier, not the middle.

items.fbDefault: Look at the 3rd value in the sorted list: 40, 42, 44, 46, 98.

items.q: Which measure is fairer for a typical stunt by Max?

options.t: The median (44), because the 98 outlier pulls the mean way above four of his five scores
The mean (54), because it ignores the 98
options.fb: The mean uses every score, so 98 pulls it upward.

options.t: The maximum (98), because it shows his best stunt
options.fb: A single best score does not show what is typical.

gates.pass: Max's typical stunt is 44, not 54. One lucky 98 cannot fool the median!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Rank the Stunts
hints: Conceptual: sort first, average the middle two for an even count, and remember the median resists extreme high or low values.
Procedural: write 62, 68, 70, 78, 84, 90 in order, then average the 3rd and 4th numbers.

steps: If 50 changes to 500, the middle pair is still 30 and 40, so the median stays 35.
worked.q: If 20 in that set changed to 2, would the median change?

items.label: Median of 90, 62, 78, 70, 84, 68:
items.aria: median of the six qualification scores

fb.msg: 78 is one of the two middle scores (70 and 78) — and was middle before sorting! Average 70 and 78.
70 is only the 3rd score. With 6 scores, average the 3rd and 4th.
You found the mean instead of the median.

items.q: If the 90 in that set changed to 150, what would happen to the median?

options.t: It stays 74, because the two middle numbers (70 and 78) did not move
It jumps to 84, because the list got bigger
options.fb: Changing the top value does not change the middle pair.
That is how the mean changes, not the median.

items.q: Who had the higher typical stunt score: Dex (median 70) or Max (median 44)?

options.t: Max, because his highest score was 98
options.fb: One outlier of 98 does not make his typical stunt higher.

gates.pass: Dex takes the stunt rank title with a median of 70 — and Blink already queued the replay!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-3 — what the stunt rank taught us
rows: Always order numbers from least to greatest before looking for the middle. Unsorted middles are not the median.
For an odd count, the median is the exact middle value. For an even count, average the two middle values.
One giant or tiny outlier drags the mean, while the median stays steady with the middle of the data.
The median is a measure of center that splits the ordered data in half — half at or below it, half at or above it.
journal.quote: "Sort the scores first, or your best replay is just a bad guess." — Mei

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-3 (Describe the Data Using the Median) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: ordering data to find the median, odd vs. even counts, and why the median resists outliers.
standards: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, using quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean)
